records.topic: rear axle position and chain slack (2019-2022 450 SX-F)
records.statement: On the 2019-2022 450 SX-F a tester moved the axle from about 608 mm to 595 mm from the swingarm pivot, which gave more front grip out of corners and less squat on acceleration. Being 2-3 mm off is fine, but 10 mm changes the bike's character. Chain slack worked best at 65-68 mm: 60 mm felt harsh, over 68 mm felt disconnected.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested: KTM 450 SX-F chain and axle position tips

records.notes: Stock gearing; model year not stated (article Sept 2021, so 2021/2022 bike). Measured centre of pivot bolt to centre of axle. For 2025 the same source suggests 600-606 mm (cd6 optional-torque record). Carried to 2019: same platform generation (2019-2022); the statement names the year it was tested or measured on where that matters.

records.topic: what moving the axle back does
records.statement: Moving the rear axle back makes the shock feel softer, because the swingarm has more leverage on it, so you may need more compression. It also lengthens the wheelbase and puts more weight on the front tire, which improves high-speed stability but can slow cornering. The 2019 swingarm was 5 mm longer than before.

source.name: Motocross Action: The long and short of moving your KTM axle rearward

records.notes: Written about the 2018.5 Factory Edition and 2019 450 SX-F; the principles apply to any linkage bike. Carried to 2019: same platform generation (2019-2022); the statement names the year it was tested or measured on where that matters.

records.statement: Testers often move to a 14T countershaft with a bigger rear sprocket (e.g. 14/52 instead of 13/49) because it settles the rear on acceleration and braking bumps. One rider reports a smaller countershaft adds squat and makes the bike easier to loft or seat-bounce. Small countershafts also wear chains faster, so going one tooth bigger in front and about three bigger at the back is common.

values.small_countershaft: more squat (single rider report), faster chain wear
values.chain: bigger combo needs a longer chain

records.topic: clutch slip and drag causes (owner reports)
records.statement: Owners with slipping or dragging KTM clutches point to a few causes: Belleville spring set flatter than the factory position (burnt plates), very short levers, worn hub rubber dampers and warped pressure plates. No single cause was agreed.

values.spring_setting: factory position 2 worked; flat burnt plates

source.name: Vital MX forum: KTM clutch observation/issue

records.notes: Thread covered a 2019 450 SX-F plus other KTMs; about 15 posters, no consensus. Carried to 2019: same platform generation (2019-2022); the statement names the year it was tested or measured on where that matters.

records.notes: 6 ft tester. Raising the fork 2 mm added front bite on entry. Stock fork soft and divey, bottoms on hills and jumps; shock soft on slap-downs. Carried to 2019: same platform generation (2019-2023); the statement names the year it was tested or measured on where that matters.

records.statement: On the 2019-2020 a tester found the stock green coupler jumpy at 0-5% throttle; the black coupler smoothed that with no loss of mid-top pull, and the white coupler plus a custom calibration-kit map filled the bottom-to-mid dip and steadied the bike in corners.

records.statement: Aftermarket slip-ons and full systems can make the 2019-2020 pop on deceleration with the green or white coupler; a tester's custom map on the black coupler cut the pops while keeping rpm excitement and adding a little mid-top pull (black alone stops pops but dulls the engine).

records.statement: Honda schedules a valve-clearance inspection every 6 races (about 15 hours). Mechanics and owners widely agree that a valve clearance that keeps getting tighter means the valve face or seat is wearing (titanium intakes most often), that the time between adjustments then gets shorter, and that the lasting fix is new valves with the seats cut, usually new springs too, rather than repeated shims. Riding type: all; dirty air filters and running on the rev limiter speed it up.

Valves are rarely reported as moving on these engines. Riding type: vet and amateur race, off-road racing.
